description: An 8-week Online Course Learn evidence-based skills to help make your caregiving sustainable. Each class has its own theme and the opportunity to practice new skills in a safe place, so they’re more available during the days ahead. Themes include: • Attentional balance and grounding • Stress responses and meeting difficult emotions • Positive intention setting • Self-compassion • Challenging relationships and patients’ concerns around “being a burden” • Re-framing chronic sorrow and ambiguous loss • Finding balance and growth in adversity • ‘What works for me?’ -- wellness practice - journals to cultivate a positive mindset Wednesdays, 9/16/26 - 11/4/26 9:30 – 11:00 AM PST Cost: Free - Registration required by 9/19 Limited to 23 participants, minimum of 5 To Register: https://scno2026.eventbrite.com Or contact: Gayle.Kojimoto@ucsf.edu | 415.509.8645 About the Facilitator Judy Long is a palliative care chaplain and educator at UCSF with a deep commitment to care for caregivers, both family members and clinicians, based on her experience in hospital and hospice chaplaincy and facilitating grief and family caregiver support groups. description: Exercise can improve physical functioning in cancer patients. It can reduce the feelings of fatigue, depression, nausea and weakness that can arise during and after cancer treatment. The UCSF Core and More class includes Pilates-based mat exercises to work on core strength and stability. We use rollers, bands and body weight as tools to enhance range of motion, flexibility, balance and muscular strength. Our goal is for you to have fun and increase your ability to perform daily activities. This class is sponsored by the UCSF Cancer Resource Center. It is open to current UCSF cancer patients and survivors. Registration is required for this class. To participate, you must undergo a pre-screening with an exercise counselor. For more information, call (415) 502-5547. There may be a waitlist for this course.

description: Session Overview This hands-on workshop focuses on how to best start basic literature searching using a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools. Discussion will cover questions to consider that guide whether an AI tool, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Consensus, and Perplexity, can be helpful in the literature searching process. Participants will practice searching a combination of databases, search engines, and AI tools to critique the results. There will be time for questions and discussion throughout the workshop. Learning Objectives Determine where AI tools may fit into the literature searching workflowCompare and contrast answers provided by databases vs. AI toolsCreate prompts to optimize AI tool answers to compliment database searchingRegister to receive the Zoom link and password. description: Osher WISE Course: What Should I Take? Making Informed Choices About Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Wednesdays, October 7–28, 6:00-7:30 p.m. PT Approximately 1 in 5 adults uses a plant-based herbal supplement, and 1 in 2 uses a vitamin or mineral product. Many people do not tell their health care providers about the supplements they are taking. This communication gap can increase the risk of interactions with prescription medications, existing health conditions, and other treatments. As the use of dietary supplements continues to grow, it is important for people to understand how to evaluate these products, recognize their potential benefits and risks, and identify which supplements are supported by strong scientific evidence. Accessing reliable, evidence-based information can help everyone make safer, more informed decisions about their health. This four-week course will help participants learn essential tips for dietary supplement selection and evidence-based information on the effectiveness and potential risks for supplements and herbals commonly used for longevity, heart health, bone health, and other uses. This course is chaired by UCSF Clinical Pharmacy Faculty, Dr. Candy Tsourounis and Dr. Cathi Dennehy. October 7: Dietary Supplements and Herbal Medicine Essentials: What You Need to Know October 14: Supplements for Healthy Aging: What's Popular, and Should I Take It? October 21: Longevity: Can Supplements Help You Live Longer and Healthier? October 28: Vitamins and Minerals: What Makes Sense for You Register here Our educational programming, formerly known as Osher Mini Medical School for the Public, has been reimagined as Osher WISE (Well-being and Integrative Science for Everyone). This public education program offers courses on integrative health topics that are current and compelling, providing an opportunity for community members to become active, informed participants in their own journey to health and well-being. https://osher.ucsf.edu/Osher-WISE, powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform
